| 2026-08-20 | `b569d53` | docs: AGENT_RULES.md shell safety - added section 7 (Shell/PowerShell Safety) documenting the indefinite-hang root causes and the rules that prevent them: (1) never run long-lived server processes (npm run dev/preview/vite) in the foreground - check the port with Get-NetTCPConnection first and start detached via Start-Process + poll instead; (2) never truncate native-command output with Select-Object -First/-Last (npm/node child processes inherit the stdout/stderr handles, the pipeline never sees EOF and PowerShell waits forever) - run commands bare and read the tool's captured output file; (3) avoid npx for anything that may need installing (interactive prompt hangs on stdin) - prefer local binaries or npx --no-install; (4) always pass an explicit timeout; also documented the preview server port 4173 in the technical notes | User reported a PowerShell command getting stuck indefinitely and asked for the root cause + a rule update so it never replicates. ROOT CAUSE: (1) PRIMARY - a long-lived server process (`npm run preview`/`dev`/`vite`) run in the foreground never exits, so the shell tool blocks until timeout; the @playtest delegation was instructed to "start it with npm run preview" if the port wasn't listening, which would hang exactly this way (confirmed: no listener on 4173/3000, but an orphaned Playwright driver from the cancelled task was still alive). (2) SECONDARY - `Select-Object -First/-Last` truncation in native-command pipelines: on Windows PowerShell 5.1, npm/node spawns child processes (vite workers, rollup, esbuild) that inherit the stdout/stderr handles, the pipeline never sees EOF, and PowerShell waits forever. FIX: AGENT_RULES.md gained section 7 (Shell/PowerShell Safety) with four rules - check the port before starting any server and start it DETACHED via Start-Process + poll; never truncate native output with Select-Object (run bare, read the tool's captured file); avoid npx install prompts (use local binaries / --no-install); always pass an explicit timeout. Technical notes also document the preview port 4173. Verified: tsc clean, 175 tests pass. |

Two stacked causes found by inspecting the live save (`hop_player_data` had `runsPlayed:3` + `missionsUnlockSeen:false` + `missionsSpotlightSeen:true`) and the tap overlay code. (1) SOFT-LOCK: the one-time missions-unlocked gate hides `#play-btn` via `#start-screen.missions-callout-pending` while `hasPendingMissionsUnlock()` is true (missions unlocked && !missionsUnlockSeen). The only paths that clear it are dismissing the missions spotlight or opening the missions overlay — but `maybeShowMissionsSpotlight()` bails the moment `missionsSpotlightSeen` is true, so a save where the teach fired once but the dismiss never persisted (tab closed mid-teach) could NEVER clear the gate: the play button stayed `display:none` forever and no teach would ever show again. (2) The tap-to-play overlay runs a gsap breathing timeline driven by CSS vars `--tap-fade-in 0.6s / --tap-hold 7s / --tap-fade-out 0.6s / --tap-gap 7s` — visible 8.2s, invisible 7s of every 15.2s cycle (~46% hidden), so even a healthy save can read as "no tap to play." Retuned to 0.5/3.5/0.5/1s: visible ~82% of the time, never hidden longer than a blink; button stays tappable the whole cycle (pointer-events auto). Verified live via CDP: simulated the stuck save → `missions-callout-pending` gone, play button `display:block` 186px hit rect, new CSS vars applied, opacity sampled through a full cycle (1s hidden gap only). 174 tests pass, tsc clean. |
